## TL;DR

Corrected the CLI/UI parity wording identified in review round 1. `repoos review keep <id>` only verifies and keeps the existing verdict, refreshing the handoff snapshot and lock; it does not start close-out. The user must then run `repoos done <id>`. The UI action labelled “Keep review verdict and merge” performs both operations. The docs site rebuilt successfully and the required changed-path check passed.

## Work and rationale

Review round 1 found that the first draft overstated what the CLI does. I re-read `src/commands/control-api.ts`, `src/server/routes/tasks.ts`, `src/ui-app/src/stores/repo.ts`, and the latest review report. The CLI handler sends one POST request to `/api/tasks/:id/review/keep`, reports that the verdict was kept, and exits. The route validates that the current verdict remains good-to-go and the main merge was take-main-only, refreshes the handoff snapshot, updates the task note and lock, and returns. It does not call `/done`. By contrast, the UI store’s `keepReviewAndMerge` calls that route and then `completeTask(t)`, which enqueues the close-out flow.

I revised `user-docs/cli.md` to say explicitly that the CLI command refreshes the handoff snapshot and review lock but does not start close-out. It now directs users to run `repoos done <id>` after a successful keep. The page distinguishes that CLI action from the UI’s combined “Keep review verdict and merge” action. In `user-docs/review-and-close-out.md`, I similarly distinguish the guarded UI sequence from the CLI’s single keep operation, and explain the separate follow-up command. These statements cite the specific CLI handler, server guard, and UI store implementation.

No code behavior changed. The review finding was strictly a docs parity issue, so the correction stays scoped to those two docs pages.

## Approaches tried

I read the stored round-1 report and checked the implementation path instead of inferencing command behavior from the UI label. The route name is shared between both user paths, but only the UI caller invokes `completeTask`; treating the CLI and UI as one operation caused the original wording error. I updated the wording to name each path’s exact result and next user action.

After editing, `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. As expected for this docs-only change, RepoOS skipped the full suite under its bookkeeping-only rule. I reran the VitePress docs build; it regenerated and validated `llms.txt`, `llms-essentials.txt`, and `llms-full.txt`, and confirmed the agent guide and changelog page build. Earlier in this task, both docs and landing builds passed and the redirect/LLM test selection passed 43 tests.

## Challenges and blockers

There were no implementation blockers. The VitePress build again emitted the existing warning for the unmatched sidebar anchor `/getting-started#starting-a-new-project-as-an-agent`; the site build and its LLM checks completed successfully. This correction does not touch that unrelated anchor.

## Key learnings

A shared server route does not imply identical user workflows. The CLI exposes the guarded state update alone, while the UI composes that update with the subsequent close-out request. Documentation should follow each caller through its completion behavior, especially when the UI control label includes two actions. The correct terminal sequence is now explicit: keep the verdict, then request Move to done with `repoos done <id>`.
